Benchmark / year Primary task and retrieval unit Relationship to the CortexRetrievalBench
TREC (1992–); BEIR (2021); FiQA (2018) General IR test collections; document or passage retrieval across domains. Supplies pooling, qrels, metrics, and cross-domain baselines. Cortex is finance-specific and has a shallower, incumbent-derived relevance pool.
FinQA / TAT-QA / ConvFinQA (2021–2022) Numerical and table-text reasoning with supplied report context. Evaluates reasoning after context selection; Cortex tests the upstream source-document choice.
FinanceBench (2023) Open-book financial QA over company filings; retrieval inside an end-to-end pipeline. Strong practitioner-style QA precedent, but exact-document ranking is not the isolated endpoint.
FinDER (2025) Expert financial queries with annotated supporting evidence; passage or evidence retrieval. Closely related professional-query benchmark; narrower retrieval unit than Cortex’s complete source file.
FinAgentBench (2025) LLM-guided document-type selection followed by passage retrieval. Closest agentic retrieval analogue; it selects a document type and then retrieves passages, rather than ranking exact files within a heterogeneous document pack.
T2-RAGBench (2026) Corpus-level retrieval of text/table context before numerical reasoning. Text-table RAG evaluation built from oracle-context QA data; not an authority-selection benchmark.
RARE / RedQA (2026) Redundancy-aware evaluation using fact-level evidence across finance, legal, and patent corpora. Shares Cortex’s pooling and alternate-evidence caveat; evaluates evidence sufficiency, not exact-source authority.
LEDGER (2026) Page-level KPI retrieval across 4,999 annual reports with TREC-style judgments. Deeply judged; narrower in source-document type and retrieval granularity.
FinRank (2026) Passage retrieval and reranking over 10-K/10-Q filings from 22 companies, with entity, period, and disclosure-context hard negatives. Closest provenance-sensitive comparator; it ranks passages within filings, while Cortex ranks complete files across mixed document functions.
FinMRAGBench (2026) Multi-document, multimodal financial RAG over annual reports; 887 expert-verified QA pairs. Broader evidence integration and end-to-end RAG; Cortex isolates exact-file authority.
LOFin / HiREC (2025) Hierarchical document and passage retrieval over 145,897 SEC filings and 1,595 QA pairs. Major scale precedent for document-first retrieval; standardized filings and end-to-end QA rather than exact authority selection across mixed source types.
FinDoc-RAG (2025) RAG evaluation over 600+ questions from 46 heterogeneous documents, all from UBS entities. Strong enterprise-document precedent within one institution; Cortex adds cross-company source packs and isolates exact-file authority.
OmniEval (2025) Chinese-language financial RAG evaluation across five task classes and 16 topics. Broadly evaluates retrieval and generation across topics and task types; Cortex isolates English exact-document authority selection.
FinTMMBench (2025) Temporal-aware multimodal RAG over tables, news, stock prices, and charts from NASDAQ-100 companies. Strong temporal and cross-modal comparator; it evaluates retrieval and analysis across modalities rather than exact source-file authority.
FinRAGBench-V (2025) Bilingual visual RAG over text, tables, and charts with page- and block-level visual citation. Important visual-retrieval and citation precedent; Cortex scores complete source documents rather than visual evidence blocks.
